record.original_question: Fix positive integers n and t, an integer m with 1≤m≤2^n−1, and an n×m binary matrix A whose columns a_1,…,a_m are distinct nonzero vectors in {0,1}^n. For an n×t binary matrix x=(x_1^T,…,x_t^T), define the i-th expressiveness indicator by m_i^A(x)=Σ_{j=1}^t <a_i,x_j>_2, where the inner product is taken in GF(2) and the outer sum is taken over the integers. If x and y are sampled uniformly at random, the computational problem asks for P((m_i(x)=m_i(y)) for all i). For fixed m and k≤m, determine this probability when A consists of all binary vectors of weight at most k.

evidence.quote: Fix n, t ∈ Z+ and let 1 ≤ m ≤ 2^n − 1. ... A = (aT1, . . . , aTm) where ai ∈ {0, 1}^n for 1 ≤ i ≤ m. Moreover, the {ai}mi=1 are non-zero and pairwise distinct.

Definition 2.2 (Expressiveness Indicator). Given A, x as above and 1 ≤ i ≤ m, we define the ith expressiveness indicator mAi (·) as: mAi (x) := Σ^t_j=1 <ai, xj>2 where the inner product <·, ·>2 is mod 2 but the outer sum is integral.
Computational Problem. Given A, let x and y be sampled uniformly at random. Compute: P ((mi(x) = mi(y)) ∀i)
Open Problem 2.1. Fix m and k ≤ m. Can we answer Computational Problem when A consists of all vectors of weight at most k?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix positive integers $n$ and $t$, and an integer $k$ with $1 \le k \le n$. Let $A$ be the $n \times m$ binary matrix whose columns are exactly all distinct nonzero vectors of $\{0,1\}^n$ having Hamming weight at most $k$; here $m = \sum_{j=1}^{k}\binom{n}{j}$. Denote the columns of $A$ by $a_1,\dots,a_m \in \{0,1\}^n$.

For an $n \times t$ binary matrix $x$ with columns $x_1,\dots,x_t \in \{0,1\}^n$, define the $i$-th expressiveness indicator by
$$m_i^A(x) \;=\; \sum_{j=1}^{t} \langle a_i, x_j\rangle_{2},$$
where $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_2$ denotes the inner product in $\mathrm{GF}(2)$ (so each summand lies in $\{0,1\}$) and the outer sum is taken in $\mathbb{Z}$ (so $m_i^A(x) \in \{0,1,\dots,t\}$).

Let $x$ and $y$ be independent $n \times t$ binary matrices, each chosen uniformly at random from $\{0,1\}^{n\times t}$. Determine, as an explicit function of $n$, $t$, and $k$, the collision probability
$$P\!\left(\,m_i^A(x) = m_i^A(y)\ \text{for all } 1\le i\le m\,\right).$$
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a 2023 survey on open problems in applied combinatorics. A web search did not turn up a published resolution; related work on commutative quantum-circuit expressiveness (e.g., arXiv:2404.19727, arXiv:2410.19173) studies the general framework but does not address the weight-at-most-$k$ case explicitly. The status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Expressiveness of Commutative Quantum Circuits: A Probabilistic Approach
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates frame potential and expressiveness of commutative quantum circuits encoded by binary matrices A, but does not specifically resolve the weight-at-most-k case.
status_evidence.claim: Related follow-up work does not appear to settle the specific weight-at-most-k computational problem.

status_evidence.title: Probabilistic Representation of Commutative Quantum Circuit Models
status_evidence.snippet: Continues the probabilistic framework for commutative quantum circuit expressiveness without addressing the specific open problem on A being all vectors of weight at most k.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the weight-at-most-k variant is given.
